title: Unsound unsafe in NoAckReceiver::receive - aliased mutable reference
description:
Location: /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/no_ack.rs lines 249-252

The unsafe block creates a soundness hole:
```rust
let packet = unsafe {
    core::slice::from_raw_parts(self.storage.as_ptr(), self.received_len)
};
```

The SAFETY comment claims 'storage was borrowed with lifetime 'a, so this is safe' but this is incorrect.

Problem: The method signature is `fn receive(&mut self, ...) -> NoAckResult<'a>`. After receive() returns:
1. The &mut self borrow ends
2. The returned NoAckResult<'a> contains an &'a [u8] pointing to storage
3. The caller can call reset() or receive() again on &mut self
4. Those methods mutate storage while the &'a [u8] from step 2 is still live
5. This creates mutable+immutable aliasing = undefined behavior

What goes wrong: Caller can do:
```rust
let result = receiver.receive(&frag);  // result.packet is Some(&[u8])
receiver.reset();  // mutates storage - UB!
// result.packet now references mutated memory
```

Fix: Either return a lifetime tied to &self (requires signature change), or use an explicit 'borrow' pattern that consumes/reborrows the receiver.
